issues.legal_issue: A tenant who remits rent by postal money order within the statutory payment period is not in default for two months merely because the tenant did not first tender the rent personally and obtain the landlord’s refusal.
material_facts: The eviction claim included rent default under the applicable rent-control law.
The tenant had not paid the rent for September, but remitted the rent for October by postal money order on November 28, within the period for paying October’s rent.
The tenant’s evidence of personal tender was not accepted, and there was no established personal tender followed by refusal.
After accounting for the timely October remittance, only one month’s rent remained unpaid.
issues.conclusion: The timely money-order remittance counted as payment for purposes of determining arrears, so the tenant was not in arrears for two months and could not be evicted on the rent-default ground.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11(1)(d) of the Bihar Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1947 makes a tenant liable to eviction when two months’ rent remains unpaid beyond the prescribed deadline, while Section 13(1) permits remittance by postal money order. Read broadly and consistently with the protective purpose of rent-control legislation, these provisions do not require a tenant to make a personal tender and prove refusal before remitting rent by money order within the payment period. The Court relied on the Full Bench decision in Raj Kumar v. Uchit Narayan, which recognized that a tenant may remit rent by money order within the deadline to avoid being treated as a defaulter.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: A landlord sought eviction of a tenant on the ground of unpaid rent in a proceeding governed by rent-control law.
predicates.rent_remitted_by_money_order_within_paym: The tenant sent rent to the landlord by postal money order before the deadline for paying that rent.
predicates.fewer_than_two_months_rent_remained_unpa: After accounting for rent remitted within the payment period, fewer than two months of rent remained unpaid.

issues.definition: When a rent-control eviction proceeding involves timely money-order remittance and fewer than two months of rent remain unpaid, the tenant is not evictable for rent default.
